current_build_blockers.title: Unresolvable transitive WebRTC artifact
current_build_blockers.evidence: app/build.gradle:94 pins com.github.team-telnyx:telnyx-meet-android-sdk:0.3.1@aar (JitPack); the SDK POM declares org.webrtc:google-webrtc:1.0.32006 compile-scoped. versions.gradle:13,71 declares deps.webrtc but app/build.gradle never uses it directly - it arrives transitively. App code imports org.webrtc.*: ParticipantTileAdapter.kt:13-14, RoomsViewModel.kt:38-39, RoomFragment.kt:41-42, SharingFullScreenFragment.kt:21, layouts participant_tile_item.xml:19, room_fragment.xml:38, sharing_full_screen.xml:9.
current_build_blockers.status: Not resolvable from Maven Central or Google Maven (404 verified at scout time); historically hosted on JCenter, which is retired. Build fails at dependency resolution before any task runs.
current_build_blockers.honest_blocker_note: This cannot be fixed by adding repositories alone. It requires one of: SDK upgrade to a maintained release, a class-compatible substitute, or self-hosting the exact artifacts. App imports of org.webrtc.* must keep compiling (or be migrated with the adapter) whichever option is chosen.

current_build_blockers.title: Unresolvable transitive libyuv artifact
current_build_blockers.evidence: Same SDK POM (compile scope); no direct references in app source (grep across repository shows zero app-side libyuv imports).
current_build_blockers.status: Not resolvable from Maven Central (404 verified); historically hosted on JCenter, which is retired.
current_build_blockers.honest_blocker_note: Rides along with whichever fix is chosen for B1. Because no app code references libyuv directly, a resolvable replacement for the SDK's frame-processing dependency carries lower risk than B1, but the SDK's compiled code must still be able to load it.

current_build_blockers.title: Configuration-time hard loads of credential files
current_build_blockers.evidence: build.gradle:33-34 loads github.properties via FileInputStream unconditionally at configuration time; app/build.gradle:10-11 loads local.properties unconditionally; app/build.gradle:36-41 throws GradleException if local.properties is unreadable.
current_build_blockers.status: A clean checkout without either file cannot even configure. Today this is masked only because both files are tracked in git (see B6).
current_build_blockers.honest_blocker_note: Fixing credential hygiene (B6) without making these loads conditional would break CI and fresh clones; the two fixes must land together or in that order.

current_build_blockers.title: Toolchain inconsistencies
evidence: gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties:4 pins Gradle 7.2 while AGP 7.1.3 (build.gradle:17, versions.gradle:4) sits at its minimum; no headroom for Kotlin Multiplatform / Compose Multiplatform plugins.

Two Kotlin Gradle plugin versions on one buildscript classpath: 1.8.22 (build.gradle:3,18) and 1.5.10 via deps.kotlin.plugin (build.gradle:25; versions.gradle:7,95). Gradle silently resolves the conflict; the catalog must unify this.
compileSdkVersion 34 (app/build.gradle:14) exceeds what AGP 7.1.3 supports (max 32); needs AGP 8.x or an explicit suppression flag. buildToolsVersion "30.0.3" (app/build.gradle:15) is stale.

Dynamic versions break reproducibility: com.bugsnag:bugsnag-android-gradle-plugin:5.+ (build.gradle:22; versions.gradle:58), com.bugsnag:bugsnag-android:5.+ (also transitive via SDK POM), androidx.core:core-ktx:+ (app/build.gradle:168).

jcenter() repositories (build.gradle:8,41) are retired; mavenLocal() (build.gradle:43) and duplicated JitPack blocks (build.gradle:10,12,44) undermine reproducibility; resolutionStrategy.force objenesis (build.gradle:48-50) is a band-aid.
Duplicate Material versions: deps.material 1.2.1 (versions.gradle:11,68) vs hard-coded 1.6.0 (app/build.gradle:130).

kapt (app/build.gradle:4) with Hilt 2.48 (versions.gradle:24); dagger 2.16 entries exist but are unused (versions.gradle:152-157); versions.kotlin=1.5.10 mixed with kotlin-stdlib-jdk7:1.8.22 (app/build.gradle:169).
current_build_blockers.status: None of these alone blocks resolution today, but each is a reproducibility or future-compatibility hazard that must be resolved before or with the KMP migration.

current_build_blockers.title: Credential exposure in version control
current_build_blockers.evidence: git ls-files tracks local.properties and github.properties despite .gitignore:24 listing local.properties (ignore rules do not untrack committed files; github.properties is not in .gitignore at all). local.properties carries API_KEY, ROOM_ID, sdk.dir; values are non-placeholder-shaped and must be treated as exposed, with an earlier 11-char API_KEY value visible at commit b520ec2 (chore: add local property). github.properties carries gpr.usr/gpr.key and currently holds only <GPR_USR>/<GPR_KEY> placeholders, but the tracked-credentials pattern must not survive the migration. The API key is additionally baked into BuildConfig and a string resource: app/build.gradle:44-46 (release) and :54-56 (debug) buildConfigField API_KEY + resValue('string','api_key',...), consumed by NetworkModule.kt:29 (BuildConfig.API_KEY).
current_build_blockers.status: Rotation of the Telnyx API key is mandatory (history cannot be silently rewritten out of scope); no values are reproduced in this evidence.

safe_kmp_compose_module_topology.principle: Module boundaries mirror the mission's capability-aware meeting contract; commonMain stays free of android.*, java.*, UIKit, and org.webrtc imports; platform SDKs enter only through expect/actual adapters and platform source sets.

modules.role: Shared Compose Multiplatform UI and navigation; hosts expect declarations for the meeting engine and publishes capability state.
Capability-aware meeting contract: suspend/Flow APIs, StateFlow UI state, buffered one-off effects; no platform imports.
Ktor client + kotlinx.serialization; repositories as interfaces; no Retrofit/Gson in common code.
androidMain actual of the meeting engine over the Telnyx Android video SDK; owns camera, audio, lifecycle, permission, screen-share integration.
iOS app consuming the shared framework; TelnyxVideoSdk pod via KMP CocoaPods interop; owns permission, audio-session, camera integration.

safe_kmp_compose_module_topology.android_entry: Keep the legacy :app (ViewBinding/Fragments) as an interim regression shell until :composeApp reaches workflow parity; acceptance gates then run against :composeApp. This preserves supported Android behavior while the shared UI is built.
constraints: commonMain forbids android.*, java.*, org.webrtc imports (architecture gate from acceptance-gates.json: common-boundary).
No LiveData, Retrofit callbacks, GlobalScope, or unmanaged CoroutineScope in common production code (coroutine-boundary gate).
settings.gradle must move to pluginManagement + dependencyResolutionManagement (FAIL_ON_PROJECT_REPOS) so module repositories stay pinned centrally.

options.detail: Move app/build.gradle:94 to a maintained Telnyx video SDK release whose POM resolves from supported repositories; verify API deltas against app usage before adopting.

Exclude the unavailable transitives from the SDK dependency and substitute a resolvable, maintained org.webrtc-compatible build; must verify package/class compatibility with the SDK's compiled code before acceptance (silent behavioral drift is the risk).

Publish the exact historical coordinates (org.webrtc:google-webrtc:1.0.32006, io.github.zncmn.libyuv:core:0.0.8) to the fork's GitHub Packages and add that repository; zero behavior change, credentials injected via CI environment (never committed - see local.properties remediation).

dependency_substitutions_or_abstractions.recommendation: Prefer A; fall back to C for zero behavior change; treat B as last resort. Gated by a dependency-resolution check with --refresh-dependencies so stale caches cannot mask failure.

dependency_substitutions_or_abstractions.detail: Pin an exact bugsnag plugin and client version in gradle/libs.versions.toml; verify plugin compatibility with the upgraded AGP before adoption.
Pin to the catalog version; dynamic last-version selection is incompatible with the reproducibility requirement.
Abstract repository data access behind interfaces in :core:network; implement with Ktor + kotlinx.serialization in shared code. Retrofit/Gson may remain in legacy :app only during the interim.
Android-only permission helper; replace with a capability abstraction (expect/actual or Moko Permissions) so common code depends on interfaces only and iOS can express honest capability state.

jobs: dependency-resolution: warm Gradle cache, ./gradlew help + classpath resolution with --refresh-dependencies; fails on any unavailable artifact (proves acceptance-gates dependency-resolution).

static-analysis: upgraded Qodana + SARIF upload (proves documentation/review assist).
secret-scan: gitleaks history scan + tracked-credentials check that fails if local.properties/github.properties are ever committed again (proves credential-hygiene).
branch-isolation: asserts only the fork's kmp-fast-vm-test branch was mutated (proves branch-isolation).
proposed.action_pins: actions/checkout@v4, setup-java@v4 (temurin 17), gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4 (cache), upload/download-artifact@v4; retire ubuntu-18.04 runners; keep tests.yml as the Firebase device matrix and extend API levels there.
proposed.secrets: API_KEY, ROOM_ID, SERVICE_ACCOUNT, GitHub Packages credentials passed via environment variables only; no step may echo secret values into logs or write them to tracked files (replaces .github/workflows/firebase.yml:29-32 pattern with a write to the now-untracked local.properties, or preferably Gradle properties/env).

local_properties_remediation.detail: git rm --cached local.properties github.properties (keep working copies; no history rewrite in scope). Values already in git history - including the earlier 11-char API_KEY at commit b520ec2 - remain exposed there.
Extend .gitignore (line 24 already lists local.properties) with github.properties, google-services.json, *.jks, *.keystore, .env so the pattern covers all credential channels.
Add local.properties.example and github.properties.example with <REDACTED>-style placeholders and a docs guide on obtaining Telnyx API keys and room IDs. No real values in any example.

Treat committed API_KEY/ROOM_ID values as compromised and rotate the Telnyx API key via the portal. Rotation is mandatory because git history retains earlier values; history rewriting is out of scope for the fork.

build.gradle:33-34 and app/build.gradle:10-11,36-41 must tolerate missing files and fall back to Gradle properties or environment variables (CI passes API_KEY/ROOM_ID via env). Remove resValue('string','api_key',...) (app/build.gradle:46,55) so the key stops landing in merged resources; prefer runtime injection into NetworkModule (app/src/main/java/com/telnyx/meet/di/NetworkModule.kt:29) through a config provider.
Secret-scan job fails the build if tracked credential files reappear; evidence records git ls-files proving untracked state. No secret value ever enters reports, examples, or this file.

work_packages.title: Clean-checkout verification and evidence
work_packages.objective: Re-run every gate from a clean clone (no local caches), record build/test/dependency-resolution logs, capture git-index proof of untracked credentials, verify freeze-manifest digests remain byte-identical, and assemble the final build-system evidence pack for review.

work_package_disjointness.note: Path-prefix write sets are pairwise disjoint by construction; no two packages may write the same path prefix.

open_questions: Which maintained Telnyx SDK release (option A) matches the 0.3.1 API surface used by the app; required before WP-B3 can close B1.

Whether the fork is permitted to publish historical WebRTC/libyuv artifacts to its own GitHub Packages (option C) under licensing constraints - WebRTC sources are BSD-style but artifact redistribution must be checked.
Target Kotlin/Compose Multiplatform/AGP/Gradle version pins must be chosen together (D6) so the plugin matrix is actually compatible.
honesty_notes: The WebRTC and libyuv failures are transitive consequences of the pinned legacy SDK artifact, not of the app's direct dependency list; versions.gradle declares the WebRTC coordinate but the SDK POM is what actually pulls it.
github.properties currently contains placeholders, not live values; it is listed as a blocker for its build-breaking unconditional load and its tracked-credentials pattern, not for leaked secrets.

The committed local.properties values were not reproduced, quoted, or hashed here; they are treated as exposed on the basis of their non-placeholder shape and history, which is why rotation (not just untracking) is required.
No migration code was written; every recommendation above is scoped to build system, dependencies, CI, and credential hygiene.
